item: Gizmodo report on SMART (Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories)
finding: Gizmodo reported on the FAA's SMART system, an $875 million effort drawing on about 200 data feeds. The report itself is real. The Nov. 10 Gizmodo article is still online and describes that expansion and those figures, citing the FAA and Ars Technica. This confirms that the report exists, not that SMART caused today's outage. [Gizmodo](https://gizmodo.com/the-faa-is-rolling-out-its-ai-air-traffic-tool-nationwide-2000839347)
label: C

finding: No evidence links SMART to the failure. It was expanded to all 22 en route centers three days earlier. Mullin said CISA is "looking at that." Vendor Air Space Intelligence posted on X that the ground stop "is not based on or a result of the SMART system." SMART only advises, and FAA specialists review every recommendation.
label: R

finding: A non-story. The Bloomberg quote was most likely a subscriber alert or social post echoing FAA Command Center wording about ATC frequency impacts, not new reporting.
label: D

item: D.C. National reporting multiple frequency outages
finding: Reagan National was held under the national stop, which is confirmed. That is consistent with the Potomac Approach SWANN/AGARD stops at 3:31 PM and the Washington Center frequency stops at 3:33 and 3:41 PM, per IFR Meter. A 4:14 PM Reagan National arrivals stop for "gridlock" is IFR Meter only and was not found in numbered advisories. A unique tower failure, and the specific frequencies named in an r/aviation post, remain unconfirmed. [ARLnow](https://www.arlnow.com/2026/11/13/developing-flights-halted-at-reagan-national-and-dulles-amid-nationwide-faa-ground-stop/) · [IFR Meter](https://ifrmeter.com/blog/national-ground-stop-2026-11-13)
label: R
